title: The Shepherd
backstory: Before David was king, he was the youngest son at home, out keeping his father's sheep (1 Samuel 16:11). In those fields a lion came, and a bear, and he went after them and pulled the lamb back out of their mouths (1 Samuel 17:34-35). Years later the LORD said to him, thou shalt feed my people Israel (2 Samuel 5:2). In Psalm 23 that shepherd turns it around and calls the LORD his own shepherd, the one who leads him so that he shall not want.

passages.synopsis: David calls the LORD his shepherd and says he shall not want. The shepherd leads him to green pastures and still waters and restores his soul. Even in the valley of the shadow of death there is no need to fear, because the shepherd himself is there. Goodness and mercy follow him all the days of his life.

David calls the LORD his light, his salvation, and the strength of his life. With such a God, there is no one left to fear. He asks for one thing above all — to dwell in the house of the LORD and behold his beauty. In the day of trouble, God hides him safe in his pavilion.

David keeps praying even when the way is hard. When God says seek my face, David answers that his heart will seek it. Even if father and mother forsake him, the LORD will take him up. The psalm ends with brave words — wait on the LORD, and be of good courage.

scrambleVerses.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He maketh me to lie down in green pastures:
and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

triviaQuestions.question: Where does the shepherd make the psalmist lie down?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Psalms 23:2 — "He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters."

triviaQuestions.question: Why does David fear no evil in the valley of the shadow of death?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Psalms 23:4 — "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me."

triviaQuestions.question: In Psalm 23, what runneth over?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Psalms 23:5 — "Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over."

triviaQuestions.question: Psalm 27 calls the LORD my light and my what?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Psalms 27:1 — "The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?"

reflection: David knew the LORD as a shepherd who provides, leads, and stays close even in the darkest valley. Where do you need to trust the Shepherd's care this week?
